correctness.rationale: For selected vertices listed cyclically, a gap >2r+1 has an undominated interior vertex. Two gaps >r disconnect the induced selected subgraph; conversely all short gaps or exactly one long gap form a connected spanning chain. Anchor-gap counting divides n ordered-rooted tuples by k, giving [z^k]Q=(n/k)[u^n]A^k+n[u^n]BA^(k-1). The maximum allowed total rk+r+1 gives k_min=ceil((n-r-1)/r), and stars-and-bars deficits give n*binom(k+r-d,r+1-d); 2r omitted vertices sharply obstruct large-set saturation. Independently checked adjacency/BFS vs coefficient formula in small n,r; the all-parameter argument is combinatorial, not experimental.
residual_risks: Finite brute graph checks cannot certify infinite n,r; proof relies on circular-gap equivalence.

evidence: Galvin and Zhang, The domination polynomial of powers of paths and cycles (arXiv:2408.12731): Counts ordinary dominating subsets; does not impose induced-subgraph connectivity or the one-long-gap count.
Mojdeh and Emadi, Connected Domination Polynomial of Graphs (DOI:10.1515/fascmath-2018-0007): Already gives ordinary-cycle r=1 polynomial, correctly treated as known; no general r cycle powers.

Caputi, Celoria and Collari, Categorifying connected domination via graph überhomology (arXiv:2201.00721): Relates polynomial to homological construction; unverified as complete coefficient formula for all C_n^r.
broader_coverage.reasoning: Galvin–Zhang ordinary domination polynomial is a superfamily of eligible vertex sets, but counting supersets alone does not imply the connected subfamily; Caputi graph homology supplies a framework without this exact evaluation.

value.rationale: Connected domination of cycle powers is a natural graph invariant. The all-n,r size distribution with a simple exact gap characterization, minimum-set multiplicity and sharp saturation threshold goes meaningfully beyond a single easy special case; it is not merely the known ordinary domination polynomial.
residual_risks: Mathematical significance is confined to the specified natural object and precise invariant; stronger generalizations are not asserted.

limitations: A classical cyclic-run or circulant enumeration could give the equivalent full two-parameter formula, even without the term connected domination.
Finite brute graph checks cannot certify infinite n,r; proof relies on circular-gap equivalence.
